title: Vijai Pal v. State of U.P.
coram: Sunita Agarwal, J.; Vipin Chandra Dixit, J.
disposition: Writ disposed; clause 6.5 representation to Executive Engineer directed.
headnote: Electricity grievances raised in writ are to be pursued by representation to the Executive Engineer under clause 6.5 of the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005. Without examining merits, the High Court disposed of the petition, directed a clause 6.5 representation within two weeks, required an expeditious decision preferably within two months, and stayed coercive measures for that period, subject to the petitioner filing the objection in time.
facts: Vijai Pal invoked the writ jurisdiction of the Allahabad High Court against the State of Uttar Pradesh and others, including the Executive Engineer of Vidyut Vitran Ltd. at Karhal Road, Mainpuri. The petition raised electricity-related grievances against the distribution licensee, in a setting that contemplated coercive recovery if no objection was filed. The Division Bench did not record the particulars of the underlying bill, demand, or connection dispute, and expressly declined to enter the merits of the petitioner's claim.

holding_units.holding: For grievances raised in the writ, the petitioner's remedy is to approach the Executive Engineer under clause 6.5 of the Electricity Supply Code, 2005. Without entering the merits, the writ is disposed of with a direction that the petitioner file a representation before the Executive Engineer, Vidyut Vitran Ltd., Karhal Road, Mainpuri, under clause 6.5 within two weeks; the competent authority shall decide it expeditiously in accordance with law, preferably within two months. No coercive measure shall be taken for two months or until that decision. Default in filing the objection within time leaves the respondent free to proceed in accordance with law.

principle_tags.application: The Division Bench held that the writ petitioner's electricity grievances were to be pursued under clause 6.5 rather than on the writ, and disposed of the petition on that footing without a merits decision.

The Court directed the petitioner to file a clause 6.5 representation before the Executive Engineer within two weeks and required an expeditious decision in accordance with law, preferably within two months.
The designated forum was the Executive Engineer, Vidyut Vitran Ltd., Karhal Road, Mainpuri, with a time-bound stay of coercive measures pending that representation.

not_decided.point: Merits of the petitioner's electricity grievances
not_decided.note: The Court expressly declined to enter the merits of the claim.
